messages:
Maya: Quick policy check — one of our teammates is going on extended medical leave and the team asked about donating PTO to them. Do we have a PTO donation program?

Olivia (People Ops): We don't have a formal donation program today, but we can do ad-hoc PTO grants as a compassionate exception. Process: manager files an exception ticket, team members transfer PTO to manager pool, People Ops reviews fairness, Payroll processes as a discretionary grant.

Ethan (Manager): Do donors lose their hours or do we create additional company-funded hours? Team prefers voluntarily donating existing PTO balances. Any legal or tax gotchas?

Legal (Counsel): Important: donating actual accrued PTO can create complex tax/employment implications depending on jurisdiction. Safer path is company-funded discretionary grant (paid from charity/discretion budget) or an unpaid donation that reduces donor balance. If you want to transfer donor balances, we need signed consent and local law check.

Kai (Payroll): From payroll: we can move hours between employees only for internal W-2 transfers if documented. For contractors, it's not possible. Also need to check minimum balances (donor can't go below 0). Cutoff for applying any grant before year-end calendar: 12/10.

Maya: So two options: 1) donors forfeit hours (not ideal), 2) company issues discretionary PTO grant funded by budget. Which is faster?

Olivia (People Ops): Option 2 is fastest and cleaner. Manager submits exception ticket with proposed grant amount and budget code, People Ops + Finance approve, Payroll applies grant. If the team insists on donor transfers, Legal must approve wording and donors must sign consent form.

Ethan (Manager): For speed, let's do a discretionary grant of up to 40 hours. I'll cover budget. What's the exact request we should put in the ticket?

Olivia (People Ops): Submit: "Request discretionary PTO grant: employee ID, hours requested (max 40), business justification (medical leave), budget code, approval from manager & finance." Attach manager email approval. We'll route to Legal for the jurisdiction check.

Maya: One more related item: part-time contractors (0.6 FTE) are asking if accrual caps apply to them and whether they can carry over unused holiday into next year. Any special rules?

Olivia (People Ops): Part-time W-2s pro-rate accruals and are subject to the same cap rules but limits are pro-rated. Contractors are paid per contract and usually not eligible for carryover. For carryover exceptions, manager + People Ops approval needed.

Legal (Counsel): Note: some states require sick carryover regardless of FTE. Check state law before denying a carryover.

Kai (Payroll): Practical note: if you approve carryover for a pro-rated employee, tell Payroll the exact hours to carry over and the grant code. We'll enter it as a manual override. Cutoff to request year-end carryover adjustments: 12/01.

Maya: Great. I'll file two tickets: one for the discretionary grant (attach budget code) and one for the carryover exception for the 0.6 FTE.

people-ops-bot: New exception tickets created: #HR-2100-001 (PTO grant) and #HR-2100-002 (carryover exception). Triage ETA 2 business days.

Olivia (People Ops): Thanks team. Maya please include employee IDs and state of employment so Legal and Payroll can triage quickly. We'll aim to complete both before the year-end cutoffs. :white_check_mark:
